CodeConvoy third-party notices
=============================

CodeConvoy's original code and artwork remain MIT licensed (see LICENSE or
LICENSE.txt). The MIT grant does not replace the terms of third-party code,
fonts, data, libraries or installer components. No additional restrictions are
imposed on recipients' rights under those licenses.

This bundle conservatively includes notices for all four release targets,
including build-time/generated-code inputs. Inclusion is not a claim that all
listed components occur in every binary. THIRD-PARTY-INVENTORY.json records
versions, license expressions, source identities, target coverage and gaps.
OR expressions retain their upstream alternatives; they do not require taking
every alternative. self_cell's Apache-2.0 alternative is used. No GPL or LGPL
alternative is selected for otherwise MIT/Apache dual-licensed Rust crates.

Unmodified option-ext 0.2.0 is covered by MPL-2.0. Its complete corresponding
source is included as option-ext-0.2.0.crate in THIRD-PARTY-SOURCES.zip. The
archive matches Cargo.lock's checksum; unpack it with a gzip/tar-capable tool.
The covered source remains under MPL-2.0. CodeConvoy is a larger work with
separate MIT-licensed source files; linking option-ext does not relicense those
files. Preserve the MPL text and source notices when redistributing.

Embedded Hack, Noto Emoji, Ubuntu and emoji-icon-font assets are unmodified.
Their copyright, font naming and redistribution conditions follow below.
Unicode data notices accompany the crates that include them. Additional Rust
standard-library copyright/Unicode notices and component versions are in
RUST-STDLIB-LICENSES.html, readable offline in a browser. Its omissions are
supplemented below from Rust 1.99.0's checksum-verified source distribution:
the library's own dependency lockfile, compiler-builtins, libm, architecture
intrinsics, unwind and other nested library notices. compiler-builtins uses
MIT AND Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, not a choice of just one of those terms.

The AppImage launcher is a separate runtime containing statically linked
third-party libraries, including LGPL-2.1 libfuse. See THIRD-PARTY-SOURCES.zip
for the available runtime/library source and patch. Source/relink completeness
and several native component identities remain unresolved below. This candidate
bundle is audit evidence, NOT a certification of complete license compliance.
Public release is blocked until the listed obligations have been resolved.
CodeConvoy imposes no restriction on modifying the LGPL-covered runtime for
your own use or reverse engineering it to debug those modifications. The full
LGPL-2.1 text and libfuse notices are reproduced below. The available source
bundle is not yet a verified section 6(a) relinking kit.

The Windows installer uses NSIS 3.09 and its LZMA decoder. Its source is
available as nsis-3.09-src.tar.bz2 in THIRD-PARTY-SOURCES.zip, together with
the CPL-1.0 terms and linking exception in the notices below. CodeConvoy
provides no additional warranties on behalf of these contributors. Any
different terms for CodeConvoy's own files are offered by CodeConvoy alone.

The installer plugin's ring dependency includes code from BoringSSL/OpenSSL:
This product includes software developed by the OpenSSL Project for use in the
OpenSSL Toolkit (http://www.openssl.org/).
This product includes cryptographic software written by Eric Young
(eay@cryptsoft.com). This product includes software written by Tim Hudson
(tjh@cryptsoft.com).
The complete upstream notices and conditions appear below. Additional plugin
dependencies and toolchain obligations remain unresolved; the recovered list
is not represented as a complete binary inventory.

Agent CLIs, Git, host graphics/desktop libraries, macOS frameworks and Windows
system DLLs are installed separately and are not bundled by CodeConvoy. The
packaging checks reject additional bundled native binaries pending review.
